long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Gomel, Andrey Melnichenko studied physics in Moscow as the Soviet Union's dissolution opened a fast-changing commercial landscape. He and fellow students started currency-exchange booths, then co-founded MDM Bank. After the bank became an established private lender, Melnichenko and Sergei Popov shifted into industrial acquisitions. They assembled fertiliser producer EuroChem and coal supplier SUEK from a collection of plants and mines.

Melnichenko approached those businesses as long-term industrial projects, investing in modern production, infrastructure and technical capacity. Through the Andrey Melnichenko Foundation, he later returned to science and education, developing regional learning infrastructure and supporting science-based sustainable development. The foundation concentrates on educational opportunity, food security and climate action, linking his early physics background with a broader programme of community investment.
